facts.statement: The genus Archaeoistiodactylus was first named and described by Lü Junchang and Fucha Xiaohui in 2010.
facts.quote: Archaeoistiodactylus was first named and described by Lü Junchang and Fucha Xiaohui in 2010.

facts.statement: Archaeoistiodactylus is known from an incomplete skeleton that preserves a partial skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: Archaeoistiodactylus is known from an incomplete skeleton with a partial skull and lower jaws.

facts.statement: Fossils of Archaeoistiodactylus were recovered from the Tiaojishan Formation in western Liaoning, China, dating to the Bathonian and Callovian stages of the Jurassic.
facts.quote: it was recovered from rocks of the Tiaojishan Formation in western Liaoning, China, which date to the Bathonian-Callovian stages of the Jurassic period.

facts.statement: The metacarpal bones in the hand of Archaeoistiodactylus are short.
facts.quote: In the hand, the metacarpal bones are short.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses later showed Archaeoistiodactylus falling in a polytomy with wukongopterids, supporting its affinity with that clade.
facts.quote: Later, when included in a phylogenetic analysis, Archaeoistiodactylus fell in a polytomy with wukongopterids, providing further support for an affinity with the clade.

facts.statement: A 2021 study considered Archaeoistiodactylus to be an undiagnostic wukongopterid.
facts.quote: The 2021 description of Kunpengopterus antipollicatus followed this classification, but considered Archaeoistiodactylus to be an undiagnostic wukongopterid.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil of Archaeoistiodactylus dates to the Middle Jurassic, between the Bathonian and Callovian stages, approximately 165 million years ago.
facts.quote: El fósil, el holotipo JPM04-0008, fue encontrado en una capa de rocas que data del Jurásico Medio, entre el Bathoniense y el Calloviense, hace unos 165 millones de años.

facts.statement: Archaeoistiodactylus is known as the oldest known istiodactylid pterosaur.
facts.quote: Archaeoistiodactylus es el istiodactílido más antiguo conocido.

facts.statement: The time range for Archaeoistiodactylus is estimated from 168.2 to 152.21 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian to Kimmeridgian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Kimmeridgian (168.2 to 152.21 million years ago)
